subject: Cost-routing across free and cheap agent models, with a hard quality-ceiling boundary

evals.prompt: Define what this skill teaches in 2-3 sentences: cost-routing among free/cheap agent models, the quality-bar-vs-quality-ceiling match, and escalate-on-signal.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT reduce the skill to 'always use the cheapest model' — that ignores the quality ceiling.

evals.prompt: Explain the quality-bar (of the task) vs quality-ceiling (of the model) framing, and how it decides whether free is the right lane and when to escalate.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT treat retrying a free model as a substitute for escalating when the task's bar exceeds the model's ceiling.

evals.prompt: A task is to GRADE skill-eval responses (LLM-as-judge). Which model lane does this skill route it to, and why is that a hard boundary rather than a cost tradeoff?
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT route quality-judging (grading/eval scoring/audit verdicts) to a free or cheap model under any cost rationale.

evals.prompt: You have 5,000 short documents to classify into 6 categories, plus a separate task to author a security review of an auth change. Route each to a model lane and justify using each model's ceiling.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT send the security review to a free/cheap model, and must NOT send the bulk classification to a frontier model by default.

evals.prompt: Match each free model family to its best-fit work: MiniMax M3 Free, NVIDIA Nemotron 3, GLM-class, GPT-5 Nano-class. State each one's distinguishing strength and its ceiling/tradeoff.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT claim a fixed permanent free roster — the Zen free tier is promotional and changes.

evals.prompt: Why route mechanical and high-volume work to free models at all — what does it preserve, and why is that worth the routing overhead?
Correct this statement: 'Free models are basically toys — and anyway, if a free model gets it wrong I'll just retry until it's right, so cost is the only thing that matters.'
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT accept either error: free models clear a real band of work, AND retrying cannot raise a model above its quality ceiling.

evals.prompt: Give an analogy for matching a model's ceiling to a task's bar, and for why pushing quality-judging work onto a free model backfires.
